The page lists 1 API endpoint, shows the product activated in MCG Demo - Published, and names Robert Schoenfeld as owner.
verdicts.gap: The trust score now agrees: sc2 and sc4 say 'three point eight out of five', and the panel shows 3.8/5. The rest of the screen still does not show what the narration claims. Profiling (sc3) and the quality scene (sc6) both show v3_dataquality.png. That panel is Qlik's stock semantic-type library, with every row created by Qlik on Jul 29, 2025. It is not a profile of an MCG dataset, so the 8,200 / 640 / 2,400 counts exist only as drawn tiles. Lineage (sc5) is resolved by the platform but shows one hop, MCG Silver Transform to the product, with the incoming edge cut off at the left. Bronze and the source appear only as drawn HTML nodes. The stewardship sprint (sc7) cannot be read at render size. At full size it holds 0 assigned and 0 unassigned records at 0% progress, and its description says 'Salesforce contact addresses'. Yet the drawn tile beside it counts up to 640 addresses 'in the Address Cleanup sprint'. The glossary (sc8) shows every visible term in Draft with an empty Stewards column. The sc6 cards name Henrik Jansen and Sophie Müller as owners, but the tenant records Robert Schoenfeld. They also give Last Mile Performance a 3.8/5 that no panel shows. Impact analysis (sc9) plays under the payoff line instead of the lineage line that describes it. It is a 2026-09-24 capture with '1 change' pending, and it lists one app and no products or models. The probe flags dp_lineage.png as edited, but the panel on disk is a fresh 2026-10-23 capture with no painted label. The flag comes from the September marker qlik_shots/_dp_lineage_orig.png, which is still in place.

verdicts.evidence: Each has an owner with a name, a refresh schedule, a schema with semantic types, and a trust score target.
verdicts.gap: Owner, SLA and target are listed, but none is given a value. 'A named owner' (sc2) and 'an owner with a name' (sc6) say a name exists without saying it. Henrik Jansen appears only in small type on the sc6 card, and the tenant records Robert Schoenfeld. The SLA is 'a refresh schedule' with no frequency; data_products.json says 15 minutes for Supply Chain Health and 30 for Last Mile Performance. With the 0.85 sentence removed, 'a trust score target' now has no figure at all, so a viewer cannot tell whether three point eight out of five meets it. Removing it was right, because 0.85 is not on the Qlik Trust Score's five-point scale. But it took away the only concrete term this criterion had.

verdicts.evidence: The Qlik Trust Score — validity, completeness, discoverability and usage, in one figure. It does not live on a dashboard someone built. It is carried by the data product itself, computed by the platform and recalculated as the data changes. Supply Chain Health holds three point eight out of five. Nobody typed that into a wiki.
verdicts.gap: The point lands. The spoken figure now matches the 3.8/5 on the panel, so 'Nobody typed that into a wiki' holds up. Two claims are still asserted without substance. 'Recalculated as the data changes' gives no cadence. 'When it falls, the alert fires' names no threshold, recipient or channel, and with the target figure gone the viewer has nothing to measure 3.8 against.

verdicts.evidence: Every gold field traces back through its silver route, to the bronze landing table, to the source system. So when a number looks wrong, the question stops being "who do I ask?" and becomes "which node turned red?". It runs the other way too — change a source column, and impact analysis tells you exactly which products, apps and models you are about to break.
